Dante Alighieri quotes

3 passages in English · 1265–1321 · medieval Christian thought.

1265–1321

medieval Christian thought

Overview

Dante Alighieri (1265–1321) was the Florentine poet-philosopher of the Divine Comedy, exiled in the Guelf–Ghibelline conflicts. He wrote vernacular epic that synthesizes Aristotelian ethics, scholastic theology, and civic passion. Monarchia and Convivio show explicit philosophical ambition. Handbook dates: 1265–1321. Exile made him Italy’s prophetic wanderer of justice and love.

Main ideas

The Comedy maps moral order: infernal contrapasso, purgatorial ascent, and beatific vision ordered by love. Will and intellect find rest in God; misdirected love generates the vices. Empire and papacy should be distinct powers coordinating earthly peace and eternal ends. Vernacular eloquence can bear highest truth. Beatrice and courtly motifs become theological allegory. Justice in the city mirrors cosmic justice.

Major works

  • Divine Comedy
  • Monarchia
  • Convivio
  • De vulgari eloquentia

Legacy

Dante defined Italian literary language and Christian epic imagination for Europe. Political theologians still argue with Monarchia. The Comedy remains a total artwork of medieval moral cosmology.
